chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, who said:

I went to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'By Allah, what affords you sitting back (from rising against the ruling authorities)?' He said: 'And why, O Sadir?' I said: 'Due to the abundance of your friends, your Shias, and your helpers. By Allah, had Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) possessed what you have of Shias, helpers, and friends, neither (the clan of) Taym nor (the clan of) 'Adiyy would have coveted it (the caliphate).' He said: 'O Sadir, and how many might they be?' I said: 'One hundred thousand.' He said: 'One hundred thousand?' I said: 'Yes, and two hundred thousand.' He said: 'Two hundred thousand?' I said: 'Yes, and half the world.'

He (Sadir) said: So he (peace be upon him) fell silent from me, then said: 'Would it be easy upon you to travel with us to Yanbu'?' I said: 'Yes.' So he ordered a donkey and a mule to be saddled. I hastened forward and rode the donkey, so he said: 'O Sadir, do you see fit to yield the donkey to me?' I said: 'The mule is finer and more distinguished.' He said: 'The donkey is gentler with me.' So I dismounted, and he (peace be upon him) rode the donkey and I rode the mule.

So we proceeded, and the time of salat arrived. He said: 'O Sadir, let us dismount to perform salat.' Then he said: 'This is marshy land; salat is not permissible in it.' So we traveled until we arrived at red ground, and he looked at a boy pasturing goats and said: 'By Allah, O Sadir! Had I Shias equal in number to these goats, sitting back (from rising against the ruling authorities) would not be permissible for me.'
And we dismounted and performed salat. When we had finished the salat, I turned towards the goats and counted them, and they were seventeen.

key_terms.الشِّيعَةِ: Shias; the committed partisans and followers of the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them)
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: Helpers and active supporters of the Imam's cause
key_terms.الْجِدَاءِ: Young goats; kids — used here as the Imam's living illustration of the true, small count of his genuinely reliable Shias
key_terms.الْقُعُودُ: Sitting back; the deliberate restraint from launching an armed uprising against unjust ruling authorities
key_terms.الْمَوَالِي: Friends, devoted followers, and loyal clients attached to the Imam
key_terms.تَيْمٌ: The clan of Taym; the tribe of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah, first claimant to the caliphate
key_terms.سَبِخَةٌ: Marshy, saline ground on which salat (prayer) is not legally permissible
key_terms.عَدِيٌّ: The clan of 'Adiyy; the tribe of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, second claimant to the caliphate

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refrain from rising against the ruling authorities despite having a large following?
ai.summary: Sadir al-Sayrafi visits Imam Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and challenges him to explain why he refrains from rising against the ruling authorities, claiming that he commands the loyalty of hundreds of thousands — even half the world. The Imam responds with silence and then, during a journey to Yanbu', demonstrates through the concrete act of counting only seventeen goats being pastured that the true number of sincere, reliable Shias is far smaller than Sadir imagines — making an armed uprising without adequate, genuinely committed support impermissible. This narration is a cornerstone text in Shia political theology regarding the conditions required before a legitimate Imam may rise against unjust rule.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan and Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Abdullah Bin Hammad Al Ansary, from Sadeyr Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! What affords you<sup>asws</sup> to sit back (not rise up against the ruling authorities)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And why (Shouldn’t I<sup>asws</sup> do so) O Sadeyr!’  I said, ‘Due to the abundance of your<sup>asws</sup> friends and your<sup>asws</sup> Shias, and your<sup>asws</sup> helpers. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Had there been for Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> what is for you<sup>asws</sup> from the Shias and the helpers and the friends, neither the (Clan of) Taym (Abu Bakr’s clan), nor (the Clan of Uday (Umar’s clan) would have been greedy with regards to it (the Caliphate)’. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Sadeyr! And how many could they (Shias) be?’ I said, ‘One hundred thousand’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One hundred thousand?’ I said, ‘Yes, and two hundred thousand’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two hundred thousand?’ I said, ‘Yes, and half the world’.

He (Sadeyr) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> was silent from me, then said: ‘Would it be light upon you if you were to come along with us<sup>asws</sup> to Yanbu?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered with a donkey and a mule to be saddled and harnessed. So I initiated and rode the donkey and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Sadeyr! What is your view if you were to prefer me<sup>asws</sup> to be with the donkey?’ I said, ‘The mule is good (for me)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The donkey is kinder with me<sup>asws</sup>’. So I descended and he<sup>asws</sup> rode the donkey and I rode the mule.

So we went on and the Salāt (time) arrived, so heasws said: ‘O Sadeyr! Descend with usasws to pray Salāt’. Then heasws said: ‘This is a marshy land, the Salāt is not allowed in it’. So we travelled until we arrived at red ground, and heasws looked at a boy pasturing goats, so heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj, O Sadeyr! Had there been for measws Shias of the number of these goats, there would not have been leeway for the sitting back (not rising against the ruling authorities) for measws’.
And we descended and we prayed Salāt. So when we were free from the Salāt, I turned towards the goats, and I counted them, and there were seventeen’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar have narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad al-Ansari from Sadir al- Sayrafi who has said the following:

“Once I went in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and said, ‘By Allah, it is your obligation not to sit (without proclaiming your leadership).’ The Imam asked, ‘Why O Sadir?’ I said, ‘Because your friends, Shi’a (followers) and supporters are so many. By Allah, were Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) to have that many Shi’a (followers) as your Shi’a, friends and supporters, no one of the tribe of Tamim or ‘Ady could dare to disturb him.’ The Imam said, ‘O Sadir, how many do you think they are?’ I said, ‘One hundred thousand.’ The Imam said, ‘One hundred thousand!’ I said, ‘Yes, in fact, they are up to two hundred thousand, and I said, ‘Half of the world (population) is your Shi’a.’

“The narrator has said that the Imam remained calm and then said, ‘Is it possible to come with us to Yanbu’?’ I said, ‘It is fine with me.’ He then asked to bring a donkey and a mule already saddled. 1 hurried to ride the donkey and he said, ‘O Sadir, can you consider to allow me ride the donkey?’ I said, ‘The mule is more beautiful and noble.’ He said, ‘The donkey is friendlier for me.’ I then dismounted and he rode the donkey and I rode the mule.

We traveled until it was time for prayer. He said, ‘O Sadir, dismount and we should pray.’ Then he said, ‘This ground is soft, prayer is not permissible here.’ We moved to a red ground and he looked to a boy who shepherded goats. He said, ‘O Sadir, were I to have as many Shi’a (followers) as the number of these goats, then it would not have been permissible for me to sit (without proclaiming my leadership).’
We dismounted and prayed. When we finished the prayer 1 turned to the goats and counted them. There were seventeen heads of goats in the flock.’”
